extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent examiners, and IP practitioners (particularly in ASEAN Member States)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on allowable pre- and post-grant amendments, corrections, support/added-matter tests, and regional work-product-sharing programmes (ASPEC, PCT-ASPEC, ASPEC AIM, bilateral PPH and validation) relevant to patent prosecution in ASEAN member states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date at which requirements must be met
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of compliance with the requirements (e.g., industrial applicability) is carried out as of the priority date of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no prior disclosure before the priority date provided the information required to carry out the claimed invention and the earlier priority application did not contain such information, incorporation of the information later into the application under review would not establish industrial applicability as of the priority date and would be considered adding new matter. (References: PCT ISPE GL, Chapter 14, Paragraph A14.01[2].8.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure for rejection based on lack of industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner objects that an application lacks industrial applicability, the applicant should be allowed to file a response and submit explanation, data or evidence to address the objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissibility of the response depends on the case; usually if support can be found in the original disclosure the examiner may consider submitted data/evidence. If the examiner upholds the rejection, the applicant may appeal to an upper administrative body or a competent court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable amendments general test
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment must fulfil two conditions to be acceptable: (1) the proposed amendment must not introduce additional subject-matter; and (2) the proposed amendment must not extend the provisional protection conferred by the patent application (with limited national exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions may be verified by applying a novelty test: no new subject-matter must be generated by the amendment. Alteration or excision of text, not just addition, may introduce new subject-matter. (Exception noted: Singapore permits extension of provisional protection for post-grant amendments only.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner acceptance considerations for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should accept amendments that restrict scope, improve clarity of the description, or amend claims in a manner clearly desirable without changing their subject-matter or scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amended application must satisfy all other filing requirements. Examiners must ensure amendments do not add content beyond the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations when claims are amended
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims have been amended, examiners should consider unity of invention, whether the description needs corresponding amendment to remove serious inconsistency, and whether all amended claims are supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If categories of claims are altered, the examiner may draw attention to potential inappropriateness of the title and/or abstract. (References: PCT ISPE GL, Chapter 20, Paragraphs 5.29–5.30; Chapter 20, Paragraph 20.09.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional subject-matter test (PSIA standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment introduces subject-matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed if the overall change results in the Person Skilled in the Art (PSIA) being presented with information not expressly or inherently presented in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PSIA test takes into account matter implicit to a PSIA in what has been expressly mentioned. If the PSIA would not directly and unambiguously derive the amended matter using common general knowledge, the amendment is unallowable. (References: PCT ISPE GL, Chapter 20, Paragraph 20.12.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'inherently' requires that missing descriptive matter is necessarily present in the disclosure and would be recognized by the PSIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherency may not be established by probabilities or possibilities; the mere fact that something may result is insufficient to qualify as 'inherent'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of amendments likely to introduce new subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding information not present in the original disclosure can introduce new subject-matter—for example, inserting that a further ingredient may be added to a composition, or specifying a particular kind of support (e.g., helical springs) when none was originally disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments are normally objected to unless the applicant can show convincingly that the feature was so well known to the PSIA in the context that its introduction is an obvious clarification, or that drawings/other disclosure would lead the PSIA to that specific feature. (References and examples cited from PCT ISPE GL and EPO Guidelines.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of later-filed examples or statements as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Later-filed examples or statements of advantage, even if not allowable into the application, may be taken into account by the examiner as evidence in support of allowability of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such evidence is used to support a positive conclusion (e.g., on inventive step), the examiner should mention this evidence in the examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on introducing further examples (chemistry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of further examples (e.g., in the chemical field) should be examined carefully because further examples may prima facie extend the disclosure beyond the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although risky for added matter, later examples might still be considered as supportive evidence, but admission as amendment is scrutinized closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing missing parts after filing and reliance on priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing drawings or parts of the description may be filed subsequently and relied on to avoid re-dating provided they were 'completely contained' in the priority document and filed within any prescribed period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such missing parts should be considered part of the 'application documents as originally filed' if these conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of prior art in the description after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: There is normally no objection to introducing further information regarding prior art by amendment after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the amendment changes how the PSIA would understand the invention or changes the nature of the problem to be solved, it may not be allowable. Inclusion of prior art that shows advantages is allowable only if the advantage would have been apparent to a PSIA in possession of that prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of data or evidence submitted after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit data or evidence after filing to address examiner objections; admission depends on field and case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as support can be found in the original disclosure (no new teaching), the examiner may consider the submitted data. If the post-filing data provides a new teaching (e.g., a selection invention without support in the application as filed), it would not be admissible. Example: claiming a specific compound merely by providing its advantages later is not allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifications and removal of lack of clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of a lack of clarity will normally not be objected to, provided the change does not extend beyond the disclosure of the application as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifications must still respect the added-matter limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade marks: amendment cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment clarifies the meaning of a trade mark or replaces a registered trade mark with a technical term, examiners must ensure the amendment does not add subject-matter not disclosed originally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care is needed because the composition of a trade-marked product may have changed over time; the amendment must not introduce new technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) applications: originally filed documents and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications, the documents originally filed in the PCT phase (normally published as WO) are those considered 'as originally filed'; amendments made in the PCT phase or on entry into national/regional phase must not add subject-matter beyond the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes amended, substitute or rectified sheets attached to the WO publication; if maintained in the national phase they must not add matter and must be carefully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications: content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject-matter of a divisional application may not extend beyond the content of the parent application as originally filed, and amendments to the divisional after filing may not extend beyond the divisional as originally filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional amendments are subject to the same added-matter constraints as parent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening claims: pre-grant vs post-grant
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no pre-grant restriction on broadening the scope of claims provided the amendment does not include matter extending beyond the disclosure as filed; post-grant amendments generally cannot broaden the scope of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure in the application as filed is broader than the claims as filed, the applicant may amend before grant to align claims with the specification. Post-grant restrictions on broadening apply in most AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of support: support requirement for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment to include subject-matter from a claim into the description is permissible, but consideration must be given whether the amended description provides required support for the claims. Each claim limitation must be explicitly or inherently supported in the originally filed disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contradictions between claims and description must be resolved by amendment. Amendments introducing a negative limitation, exclusion or disclaimer should be examined for potential new-matter issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has the initial burden of establishing that the requirements for amendment have been met, even if the applicant cites portions of the original application supporting the amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should indicate the basis in the application as originally filed for any amendments and be prepared to substantiate support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendments: effect and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant amendments, once allowed, have effect and are deemed always to have had effect from the date of grant; the test and considerations for added subject-matter are the same as for pre-grant amendments, but post-grant amendments cannot broaden claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices are similar across AMS; examine whether a post-grant amendment would extend protection or add subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments versus corrections (rectification of obvious mistakes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS allow rectification of obvious mistakes pre- and post-grant. The mistake must be 'obvious' to the competent authority (e.g., examiner) and to the PSIA: (i) that something else was intended than what appears; and (ii) that nothing else could have been intended than the proposed rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-fold test: (i) recognition there was indeed a mistake; (ii) assessment whether the proposed rectification was the only meaning that could have been intended. The finding must be made based only on the description, claims and drawings (priority documents not taken into account). Examples include linguistic, spelling, grammatical errors where meaning does not change; corrections to formulas not generally rectifiable unless correct formula was common knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and evidentiary requirements for corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Once established as a correction, the change takes effect from the date of filing as if the error had never been made; the question of added subject-matter or extended protection is not relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may need to provide evidence addressing threshold questions (why it would be obvious to PSIA that there is an error and why the correction reflects the original intention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and benefits of work-product-sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Work-product-sharing shares search and examination (S&E) results between offices to help applicants obtain corresponding patents faster and more efficiently, reduce duplication, save time and effort, and serve as useful references when producing quality reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmes facilitate reuse of S&E expertise and works (e.g., ASPEC) and may increase allowance rates and efficiency; reuse remains subject to each office's national law and final decision-making autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC Prosecution Highway (regional ASPEC use of WO/written opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC allows use of a written opinion (WO) established by the first AMS patent office to request ASPEC before a second AMS patent office, provided the WO acknowledges at least one allowable claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no longer requirement to provide a final S&E report except for Thailand. ASPEC reported an allowance rate near 95% (as of Jan 2022). Use of S&E reports from ASEAN IP Office or WO generally has no cap; ASPEC form may be required; no additional fee required.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT-ASPEC programme eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT-ASPEC allows applicants to use a PCT search and examination (S&E) report prepared by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA to expedite national phase examination/grant in participating AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programme launched 27 Aug 2019, extended until 26 Aug 2025; annual cap of 100 applications for the region; use of PCT S&E report by ASEAN ISA/IPEA; use of ASPEC form if applicable; no additional fee required (subject to national rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM (Industry 4.0) specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC Acceleration for Industry 4.0 Infrastructure and Manufacturing (ASPEC AIM) is limited to Industry 4.0–related applications and provides accelerated handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited to 50 Industry 4.0–related applications per year; committed turnaround time of six months to receive first office action if ASPEC request is made; launched 27 Aug 2019 and extended for a term (example: till 26 Aug 2023).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilateral and national PPH programmes and pairing with ASPEC
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS may enter bilateral and national Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) programmes with other patent offices; these can be paired with ASPEC to further expedite examination and grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of partner offices and programs vary by AMS; programmes may involve reuse of S&E work products from other offices (e.g., JPO, EPO, KIPO, CNIPA, USPTO, IPOS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition or validation of patents (validation programmes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some offices permit recognition/validation of patents granted in partner offices under MoUs or validation agreements, subject to eligibility conditions (e.g., first-granted in Singapore and in force; filing date thresholds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: recognition of Singapore patents in Cambodia requires patent first granted in Singapore, in-force at time of filing, filing date on or after 11 Feb 2003; often no cap and low cost. Validation of EP patents in Cambodia requires request & fees within three months of EPO grant and translations of title/abstract/claims into Khmer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide available work results from priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS require applicants to submit information about available work results related to priority applications known to the applicant, either automatically or upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is best practice to assist examiners in identifying relevant prior art while preserving the autonomy of the Office of Second Filing (OSF). Examples: Malaysia and Thailand have such requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC work-sharing filing conditions for second IP Office
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application filed in a participating AMS as a 'second IP Office' must be a corresponding application of the application considered by the 'first IP Office' and must be supported by S&E documents from that first IP Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims filed in subsequent patent offices must correspond to a sufficient extent to the allowable/patentable claims referred to in the S&E documents from the first IP Office. The ASEAN Comparative Study Report (CSR) is a tool to assess compatibility of practices across ASEAN POs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for PCT-ASPEC and ASPEC AIM
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify: PCT-ASPEC requires reliance on an international preliminary examination report or written opinion issued by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA as first IP Office; ASPEC AIM requires the first IP Office to indicate the application contains at least one IPC code qualifying for acceleration under ASPEC AIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should verify which S&E documents and classifications qualify and ensure supporting documents/forms are filed as required by the receiving office.
